Hi Aditya,

We’ve started the internal review for our Outreach renewal and a couple of things came up during the licensing sweep: our SDR/AE org is going through a territory realignment and we expect seat usage to shift by role (more AEs, fewer SDR-only seats). I’ve attached the seat export from Outreach and a quick headcount plan for Q2.

Can you share the different coverage/seat models Redwood supports for Outreach renewals (e.g., shared seats, pooled licenses, role-based bundles)? Additionally, do you offer seat reallocation credits if seats are moved between user types mid-contract? Procurement is particularly sensitive to potential double-spend during the transition.

We’re aiming to finalize vendor economics by end of month. If we can get a few concrete pricing permutations (per-seat vs. pooled + suggested bundling) that would help Acme’s finance team.

Thanks —

Hi Emma — thanks for the export and the headcount notes.

Quick answers up front:
- We support both dedicated per-seat licensing and pooled seat bundles. Pooled bundles are often the most cost-efficient when you have role churn or shared tooling (e.g., SDR/CS overlap).
- We do offer mid-term seat reallocation credits in renewals if the change is driven by a documented reorg (procurement-grade paperwork required). Credits are applied against your next invoice and are pro-rated.
- We can produce a recommended coverage model (role-based buckets + buffer) once we see utilization by role.

I’ve attached a short bundle options deck with 3 pricing permutations and an example economics worksheet. Please take a look and I’ll prepare the formal quote after Marissa confirms allowable discounts and Karthik confirms any compliance guardrails.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to confirm discount band (we typically have 10/15/20% tiers for multi-year bundles).
2) Karthik to validate SSO/KMS requirements for the private tenant we discussed earlier.
3) Acme to confirm the final headcount mapping (which users remain active vs. reallocated) — Emma, your export helps but we’ll need a role mapping.

Attachments: redwood-seat-bundle-options-2026Q1.pdf

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Aditya —
We can do 15% for 12 months and 20% for anything 18 months+. Reallocation credit: we’ll allow a one-time pool-credit equal to the lesser of (a) 3 months of the redistributed seats at the current net rate or (b) 10% of the annual contract value. Need to flag to finance for ARR treatment but it’s a standard allowance.

Karthik — please confirm there are no compliance blockers for the private tenant configuration Acme asked about.

Subject: Coverage model & seat economics — Outreach renewal (Acme Analytics)

Emma — thanks for your patience. Based on Acme’s export and our internal review, here’s a concise proposal: 

1) Recommended model (Cost + coverage):
- Pooled seat bundle: 220 pooled seats (30% buffer to cover ramp + territory changes)
- Suggested split: 150 AE-licensed seats, 40 SDR-heavy seats (with view-only), 30 floating seats for pilots

2) Pricing permutations (net after listed discounts):
- 12-month term: 15% off list, $98/user/month equivalent (annualized) — total ARR $258,720
- 18-month term: 20% off list, $92/user/month equivalent — total ARR $241,488 (saves ~6.7% vs 12m)
- Add-on: reallocation credit (one-time) equal to the lesser of 3 months of redistributed seats at net rate OR 10% of ACV (Marissa confirmed).

3) Attachments included: pricing summary (redwood-pricing-summary-2026Q1.xlsx) and the bundle options deck.

4) Operational notes:
- We will require a role mapping CSV for final quote (we can accept your export + a two-column role mapping).
- If Acme chooses private tenant, Karthik will validate KMS/SSO; that’s included in the quote but may add a one-time config fee.

Next steps:
- If this aligns, I’ll generate the formal Master Services Quote and send a DocuSign for signature (HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789012).
- Please share the role mapping by EOD Thu so we can lock pricing and get legal sign-off.
